# FDG5108

> DO validate arguments passed to public, protected, or explicitly implemented members. Throw `System.ArgumentException`, or one of its subclasses, if the validation fails.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.8.2 Validating Arguments.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1062
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

CA1062 reports a parameter of an externally visible method, protected members included, that is dereferenced without a null check. Validation in a called method counts, as the body allows: in a probe with SDK 10.0.402, a public method that passed its argument to a private method that throws ArgumentNullException was not reported. CA1062 checks only null arguments, not ranges or formats, and in that probe it did not report an explicit interface implementation, which the text names. It accepts any null check, not only one that throws an ArgumentException: a parameter that is checked and then silently ignored is not reported (see FDG5073). The Mariani annotation lets low-level comparison and hashing functions skip validation; CA1062 still reports them. CA2208 is not mapped: it checks how argument exceptions are constructed, which the chapter 7 exception rules cover. CA1062 has no code fix; adding validation changes no signature.

## From the book

```csharp
public class StringCollection : IList {
   int IList.Add(object item){
       string str = item as string;
       if(str==null) throw new ArgumentNullException(...);
       return Add(str);
   }
}
```

Note that the actual validation does not necessarily have to happen in the public or protected member itself. It could happen at a lower level in some private or internal routine. The main point is that the entire surface area that is exposed to the end users checks the arguments.
